AI's coming roadblock in regulation: Antitrust hawks
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-30
10:26:36 UTC
19:26:36 KST

The push to regulate artificial intelligence faces a big speed bump in Washington: Antitrust hawks.
AI companies have asked for narrow antitrust exemptions to collaborate on safety issues as they push Washington to regulate them amid growing fears that the technology could grow out of control. But some lawmakers on Capitol Hill who would write the laws regulating the industry are recoiling at the suggestion of an antitrust carveout.
"No," Sen. Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass., told CNBC at the Capitol when asked about a potential waiver. "Antitrust law already has an exception for companies working together on safety issues; there's no need for any additional antitrust waivers."
"I understand that big companies love antitrust waivers, but no," she said.
Warren was one of a number of antitrust exemption skeptics on Capitol Hill who CNBC spoke with to gauge the appetite for granting the request floated by Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei with support from other AI executives.
In a blog post earlier this month, Amodei raised the possibility of an antitrust waiver. The essay, titled "We Must Pace the Frontier," came after one of Anthropic's researchers resigned and said publicly that AI "could kill us all by the end of the decade."
"AI companies can and should voluntarily work together to set standards," Amodei wrote in the essay. "For antitrust reasons, it's helpful for the US government to mediate or at least enable these discussions — they don't need to participate, but do need to issue a narrow waiver for certain kinds of safety conversations."
Other AI executives quickly endorsed Amodei's call to action, setting off a mad dash in Washington to come up with rules for the technology.
But the short amount of time left this year for Congress to legislate and the bitterly divided nature of the government's legislative branch mean that any brewing dissent presents a risk to quickly passing legislation on a pivotal topic like AI.
Antitrust enforcers are also skeptical of any carveouts for AI, whose executives met Tuesday at the White House with President Donald Trump.
In addition to Amodei Google's Sundar Pichai, Tesla and SpaceX chief Elon Musk, Meta's Mark Zuckerberg, OpenAI President Greg Brockman and Jensen Huang of Nvidia appeared at the White House as Trump declared that artificial intelligence should be called "super intelligence" instead.
Jonathan Kanter, who ran the Justice Department's antitrust division under former President Joe Biden, told CNBC an exemption to existing antitrust laws is not needed for the companies to collaborate on safety.
"They can share information about malicious threats and other information without an antitrust exemption," Kanter said. "The antitrust laws don't prevent companies from coming together to talk about how to develop standards to make products more safe ... what the antitrust laws might prevent is companies coming together and saying they should stop innovating and stop competing."
Amodei described such a slowdown in his essay about pacing as collective "limits on the rate of unchecked AI progress" and noted they could be legally challenging.
"They don't need to make those decisions jointly," Kanter said.
Kanter said Congress should separately consider imposing "basic rules of the road to ensure that the public is protected from harmful products and services in this new and emerging area."
He also warned safety could be used as a pretext for the companies to coordinate on other types of anticompetitive behavior.
"There's a real risk that you can get the antitrust exemption wrong," he said. "That being said, I don't think you need one.
Kanter and Warren are not alone in saying they don't think antitrust waivers are necessary for the companies to coordinate on safety.
"They don't need a waiver to prevent catastrophic consequences as long as they're cooperating with some kind of governmental rubric or oversight," Sen. Richard Blumenthal, D-Conn., told CNBC.
And Sen. Ruben Gallego, D-Ariz. warned about the possibility that Congress could rush into delivering the AI industry everything it wants.
"I'd have to see exactly how far that goes, it doesn't remove them from liability issues, first of all," Gallego said of potential legislation. "I'm not going to give them a free carte blanche on everything."
Sen. John Hoeven, R-N.D., said Congress is still trying to figure out a coordinated way forward on addressing AI. He warned that prior experience regulating other recent technological breakthroughs like the internet looms large over lawmakers.
"I think there's unhappiness with these antitrust carveouts that the internet guys got, so we're thinking about, okay, how do we avoid that problem with AI?" Hoeven told CNBC. "To just give them some carte blanche antitrust thing, we've seen that doesn't work."
In addition to the antitrust concern, some lawmakers are suspicious of calls for a coordinated slowdown of AI, warning it could result in regulatory capture — where a regulator intended to serve the public's needs instead bends to industry. Some analysts have suggested it could be a ruse to curb the companies' growing debt portfolios ahead of initial public offerings and stifle competition, though there is not concrete evidence of such coordination.
"A little bit," Sen. Kevin Cramer, R-N.D., said Tuesday when asked about whether he's concerned about the potential for regulatory capture on CNBC's "Squawk Box." "Anything that blocks entrance to an industry by somebody who's big in it, again, I'm always a little bit suspicious of."
AI companies have some congressional support
Industry's call for a narrow antitrust exemption does have some supporters.
Reps. George Whitesides, D-Calif. and Bob Latta, R-Ohio, and Sens. Adam Schiff, D-Calif., and Jim Banks, R-Ind., carry a bill that would create such a carveout. It would allow AI companies to share information relating to AI security threats to prevent, investigate or mitigate the risk. The bill would also allow them to coordinate to reduce AI security issues by delaying or limiting the deployment of high-risk models.
"It needs to be harbored very narrowly to ensure the focus is on exactly what needs to be done around testing, evaluation and training that makes these models safer," Rep. Sam Liccardo, D-Calif., who pushed for Whitesides' bill, told CNBC. "Frankly, there's not a lot of incentive for these companies to want to collaborate on a whole lot of things; this is an intensely competitive industry."

The Swiss economy is likely to grow faster than expected
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-30
10:26:00 UTC
19:26:00 KST

The Swiss economy is likely to grow faster than expected
Economists at the KOF Institute at ETH Zurich have significantly raised their growth forecast for the Swiss economy for 2026. They are also more optimistic about the coming year. However, uncertainty remains high.
Gross domestic product (GDP) is expected to rise by 1.9% this year, excluding international sporting events, as economists announced on Wednesday. Back in the summer, they had initially expected growth of just 0.8%. The KOF Institute now forecasts growth of 1.7% for 2027 (previously 1.5%) and 1.7% for 2028 as well.
“Despite the pressures caused by US tariff policy and higher energy prices, the global economy has so far proved resilient,” the report states. The Swiss economy, too, performed significantly more robustly than expected in the first half of 2026. The strong second quarter was a particular surprise.
At the same time, the national accounts have been revised upwards, according to the data, and thus paint a “significantly more favourable picture” of recent developments. Nevertheless, uncertainties remain high due to the situation in the Middle East, US tariff policy and rising bond yields.
Rising employment expected
The labour market presents a mixed picture. A more positive assessment emerges from the revised data and the surprisingly strong second quarter. Consequently, the KOF Institute now expects job growth of 1.5% in 2026, having previously forecast just 0.5% in the summer.
On the other hand, however, unemployment remains high. According to the economists, part of the recent rise in unemployment could therefore be “structural in nature”. One factor is the increased use of AI. According to the State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO definition), the annual average unemployment rate is expected to be 3.1% cent in both 2026 and 2027.

Ex-Pakistan SSG commando, highly trained LeT terrorist, Pahalgam mastermind: Who was Hashim Moosa; killed in J&amp;K encounter
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-30
10:25:09 UTC
19:25:09 KST

Hashim Moosa (right) killed in an encounter in Jammu and Kashmir’s Budgam district
NEW DELHI: Pakistan-based Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) terrorist Mohammad Asif alias Hashim Moosa, wanted for his alleged role in the 2025 Pahalgam terror attack, was killed in an encounter with security forces in Jammu and Kashmir's Budgam district on Wednesday.Moosa was killed during a joint operation by the Indian Army, Jammu and Kashmir Police and the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) in the Korag area of Yousmarg. His body was later recovered from the general area of Palmaidan along with war-like stores, according to the Army's Chinar Corps.
Moosa's killing has brought renewed focus on the background of the LeT terrorist, who security agencies had identified as one of the key suspects in the Pahalgam attack and linked to other terror attacks in Jammu and Kashmir.
Who was Hashim Moosa?
Moosa was a Pakistani LeT terrorist wanted in connection with the April 22, 2025 Pahalgam terror attack, in which 26 people were killed.Former Jammu and Kashmir DGP S.P. Vaid on Wednesday described Moosa as a highly trained terrorist and alleged that his footprints had surfaced in several attacks in Jammu and Kashmir, including attacks in the Poonch region and the Pahalgam attack.Vaid said Moosa was considered the mastermind of the Pahalgam attack and described him as a Pakistani national and a commando-trained terrorist specialising in jungle warfare and guerrilla operations.
Is Hashim Moosa an ex-SSG commando?
One of the key aspects of Moosa's background now being examined is his alleged connection with Pakistan's military.News agency ANI also quotes security agency sources stating that Moosa had served as a para-commando in Pakistan's Special Service Group (SSG) where he held the rank of Havildar. Following his retirement from the SSG in 2023, he joined the terrorist outfit Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) and infiltrated into India.Vaid described Moosa as a highly trained commando specialising in ambushes and guerrilla-style attacks. He alleged that Moosa's footprints had been seen in attacks in Poonch, DKG, Bhimber Gali, the Gulmarg attack and the Reasi attack on pilgrims.The alleged SSG connection could shed further light on Moosa's training and his role within the LeT network, but the military background remains a matter of investigation.ALSO READ: 'Save Democracy March' announced: INDIA bloc projects unity amid SIR row, targets PM Modi, Amit Shah
What attacks is Moosa linked to?
The Pahalgam attack took place on April 22, 2025, when terrorists targeted tourists at Baisaran Valley. Twenty-six people were killed in the attack.According to the ANI report, Moosa was named as one of the key suspects in the attack and had been wanted by Jammu and Kashmir Police.The National Investigation Agency later chargesheeted seven accused in the case, including Pakistan-based LeT and The Resistance Front (TRF), which it charged as a legal entity for allegedly planning, facilitating and executing the attack.The NIA's 1,597-page chargesheet also named Pakistani handler Sajid Jatt as an accused.The agency had said its investigation detailed the Pakistan-based conspiracy and the roles of those accused in the attack.
How was Moosa killed?
Security forces launched Operation Korag in the Yousmarg area of Budgam following specific intelligence inputs about terrorist movement.During the joint search operation, troops observed suspicious activity and challenged the terrorists. The terrorists opened fire, triggering an encounter in which Moosa was killed.The operation involved the Indian Army, Jammu and Kashmir Police and the CRPF.The search operation continued after the encounter, with security personnel checking the surrounding area for any additional terrorist presence. During the search, Moosa's body was recovered from Palmaidan along with war-like stores, according to the Chinar Corps.
Pahalgam victim's daughter calls it ‘one chapter’ closed
The killing also drew a reaction from Asavari Jagdale, daughter of Pahalgam attack victim Santosh Jagdale.Speaking to ANI, Jagdale thanked the Army and intelligence agencies for the operation and recalled the April 22 attack in which 26 people were killed.She described the killing as a step towards justice but said the legal process must continue until the case reaches its final verdict.“I would say that one chapter of the case has ended,” she said.
Jagdale also urged security agencies to continue operations against terrorists and said the 26 families would consider the case fully closed only after completion of the legal proceedings.

European police forces drop Russian software firm following POLITICO probe
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-30
10:23:59 UTC
19:23:59 KST

European police forces drop Russian software firm following POLITICO probe
Authorities in at least three countries are suspending their use of Oxygen Forensics after allegations emerged about the company’s secret Russian owners.
BRUSSELS —Multiple European law-enforcement agencies will stop using Oxygen Forensics, a digital surveillance company accused of concealing its Russian ownership, after POLITICO revealed its spying services had been sold to police forces across the continent.
Romania's National Anticorruption Directorate (DNA) told POLITICO it has initiated procedures to terminate its contract with Oxygen Forensic’s "detective" software used to extract and analyze data from mobile phones in criminal investigations.
The agency's most recent annual license was purchased through a Romanian distributor on Aug. 27 for €13,000.
Advertisement
"In light of information recently made public about the company that produces this software, the National Anticorruption Directorate has initiated the necessary procedures to terminate the contractual obligations regarding this product," DNA said.
The agency added that its checks had found no evidence that data extracted or processed using Oxygen had been compromised.
Elsewhere, Latvia's State Police has suspended its use of the software while it assesses whether to continue using the technology. The police explained that officers had previously relied on it to extract and analyze electronic data, but stressed that its use "was under strict control," meaning it was isolated from employees' working computers.
In Britain, London's Metropolitan Police has paused its use of Oxygen and launched a full review. The National Police Chiefs' Council has also encouraged forces using the technology to conduct their own assessments.
Concealing control
The moves follow POLITICO reporting this week that the Virginia-based Oxygen, which the U.S. Justice Department has accused of being secretly owned and operated from Russia, participated in EU-backed digital-evidence projects and later supplied technology to European law enforcement agencies.
Other European countries that had purchased the services of Oxygen Forensics include Germany, Spain, Italy, Poland and Hungary. Police agencies from those countries have not responded to POLITICO's request for comment.
Advertisement
U.S. prosecutors allege that Oxygen's Russian owners concealed their control of the company after Moscow's full-scale invasion of Ukraine and that its technology continued to be developed and managed in Russia. The Justice Department does not allege that the software contained malicious code or was used to access customers' systems or data without authorization.
Following the revelations, political pressure is mounting. Belgian Green MEP Saskia Bricmont is calling on European governments to immediately stop using Oxygen and investigate whether sensitive information could have been exposed to Russia.
"It is particularly ironic to see that the EU has an extremely security-driven agenda while handing over the keys of its security to American and Russian companies," said Bricmont, the Greens' coordinator on Parliament's PEGA spyware inquiry.
She also criticized the European Commission for failing to act on earlier warnings from civil society about Oxygen's alleged Russian links.
A Commission spokesperson had noted earlier this week that the company was not a member of either EU-backed consortium, EVIDENCE and INSPECTr, and received no European Union funding. Still, Oxygen currently remains listed on the websites of both projects. On its own now-defunct website, Oxygen Forensics had also listed the European Commission as a client.

Minecraft hotel to open near London as gaming-themed travel goes up a level
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-30
10:22:01 UTC
19:22:01 KST

A new 69-room Minecraft hotel is coming to the UK, joining a growing crop of properties designed to let fans step inside their favourite games.
Minecraft is no longer just a game you can play – soon, it’ll be somewhere you can actually stay.
A new Minecraft World Hotel is set to open near London in 2027, giving fans the chance to sleep inside the world of the best-selling video game of all time.
The 69-room hotel will form part of Chessington World of Adventures’ new Minecraft-themed area, complete with a Nether-inspired roller coaster, immersive dining and plenty of pixelated details.
The announcement comes just as the trend for gaming-themed travel is at its peak.
Gaming-themed travel is becoming more than just a trip to a theme park or a visit to a gaming convention. Now more than ever, the hospitality industry is increasingly turning familiar game worlds into places travellers can actually stay, sleep and explore.
In Japan, MIMARU operates Pokémon-themed rooms across 10 hotels in Tokyo, Kyoto and Osaka, with interiors packed with Pokémon characters and details including themed bathrooms and kitchens.
This month, the concept went a step further, as a Poké Ball-shaped hotel has opened in Hokkaido as part of a Pokémon Sleep collaboration. The three-metre-wide pod sits beside a lake and is designed to recreate the experience of sleeping inside a real Poké Ball.
Closer to home, Spain's Magic World Resort in Oropesa del Mar has a dedicated Magic Games Hotel, with gaming-themed rooms, consoles, VR and AR areas, tournaments and a video game museum.
Now, the UK is getting involved. Located within Chessington World of Adventures’ new Minecraft World-themed area, the new hotel with 69 themed rooms – 20 upscale rooms and 49 standard options – will open its doors on an as-yet-unannounced date next year.
The hotel will also feature an immersive restaurant and potion bar, and interactive elements, and iconic creatures, colours and biomes – or regions – from the game will come to life, offering guests a chance to experience living inside the magical world.
Cube-like trees and animals will bring the Overworld to life in the reception area, while lifts inspired by Nether portals and corridors that look like mine shafts will draw guests in.
The rooms themselves will house the blocks, objects, creatures, textures, and colours characteristic of Minecraft in the real world.
Fans of Minecraft will also be able to head next door to the theme park to try out Escape the Nether, the world's first Minecraft roller coaster, which will boast both indoor and outdoor sections.
The ride will be located in Minecraft World, which will further bring the game to life, offering family attractions, dining areas and themed shops, as well as immersive Minecraft experiences.
“We’ve thought about every detail, from the scale of the blocks to how to bring the creatures and biomes to life in the real world,” said Filip Keatly Thoms, Creative Director of Minecraft Parks and Experiences at Mojang Studios, which is behind the project.
“Our goal is to create an authentic Minecraft experience and allow visitors to experience the game in a completely new way.”

Chinese-run Brussels networking club raises intelligence concerns
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-30
10:21:06 UTC
19:21:06 KST

The Global CEOs Dinner Club brings business leaders and political figures together at high-level events in Brussels and is now seeking to expand into France.
A Chinese-run networking club targeting business and political elites in Brussels bears the hallmarks of an influence and intelligence-gathering operation, a Western intelligence source has told Euronews.
The Global CEOs Dinner Club, which is now expanding to France, operates in a manner associated with China’s United Front, a Communist Party network used to promote Beijing’s interests abroad, according to the source.
The assessment comes as Belgium has recently been at the centre of several espionage probes launched by its Federal Prosecutor’s Office, including investigations into a former Chinese-Belgian researcher in the semiconductor industry and a Canadian national of Chinese origin working at NATO in Mons.
Yifei Yang, who runs the Global CEOs Dinner Club, studied in China and at a private European institute in Nice, France, before launching the organisation in Brussels last March.
French media outlet La Lettre reported last week that her activities had put at least one Western intelligence service on alert.
Asked by Euronews, one intelligence source would not confirm whether their service was investigating the case. However, after Yang’s activities were described to them, the source said they matched the modus operandi of China’s United Front.
The United Front is a decades-old Communist Party network known for promoting China’s interests through organisations and individuals abroad, while some of its activities have also been linked to the gathering of information for Chinese intelligence services.
Contacted by Euronews, Yang denied that China was behind the club, insisting that “we are neutral” and adding that its objective was to have an “impact on society” and “build sustainable business”.
Approached through Linkedin
Since last March, the Global CEOs Dinner Club has brought together business figures as well as people connected to Belgian and EU politics at events covering topics ranging from sustainability and diversity to technology and artificial intelligence.
On Wednesday evening, it was due to host a dinner entitled “China–EU EV Futures: Competition, Collaboration, and the Road Ahead” at a luxury Brussels hotel, bringing together business leaders, policymakers, technology executives and investors.
Guests included Hui Zhang, vice-president of Chinese electric vehicle maker NIO; Melanie Schuttenberg, a board member of Danish car components company TAJCO; and Ole Gerkensmeyer, CSO of Netherlands-based chipmaker Nexperia.
Yang said the organisation currently has 20 members from countries including France, Belgium, Denmark, Japan, China and Singapore. Annual membership costs €2,400 for individuals and €5,000 for companies.
“It is not all about business,” Yang told Euronews, describing the organisation as “value-driven”. She said 10% of its revenue goes to NGOs and charities.
The club’s website shows that speakers in recent months have included representatives from Belgian semiconductor research centre imec and Le Refuge, a shelter for LGBTQIA+ young adults.
Belgian senator Marie-Claire Mvumbi, who spoke at one of the club’s events on diversity, told Euronews that Yang had approached her through LinkedIn.
Mvumbi said between 30 and 50 people attended the event, which included discussions about diversity in business recruitment. “The event gave a good impression,” she said.
Yang says she hopes to expand the organisation into France and recently sent invitations for an event for female executives scheduled to take place in November at the luxury Le Meurice hotel in Paris.

How will Burnham’s national care service work – and how will it be funded?
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-30
10:17:03 UTC
19:17:03 KST

The prime minister said he wanted to create a care system that would give people ‘peace of mind’. Photograph: Sean Prior/AlamyView image in fullscreenThe prime minister said he wanted to create a care system that would give people ‘peace of mind’. Photograph: Sean Prior/AlamyExplainerHow will Burnham’s national care service work – and how will it be funded?PM has revealed more details about a proposed shake-up of adult social care – including a broad timetableAndy Burnham’s Labour conference speech gave a little more detail on how he intends to take forward what he said at the start of his premiership would be his signature social policy ambition: an overhaul of adult social care.Andy Burnham’s social care plans could be much more radicalRead moreWhat will Labour’s social care overhaul look like?Burnham was clear about the ambitious scale of his care vision – this was not simply change, it was about creating a whole new service: a “landmark policy, as significant as the creation of the NHS itself”. It would be a national care service, operating on NHS principles: free at the point of use and “where everyone contributes and everyone is covered”.It was more emphatic than his last social care speech in June, when he said a national care service “could be fully fledged [NHS-style] or lesser options or something in between”. After the speech, however, the prime minister’s aides clarified the new service would not resemble what most people would think of as an NHS-style system; it would be based on the Scottish adult social care approach: free personal care, with individuals paying for accommodation (“bed and board”) costs.Are we any clearer as to how it will be paid for?Experts say an NHS-style care system would be expensive – possibly the most expensive option – costing about £18bn a year. A Scotland-style system would cost an extra £7.5bn a year, according to the Health Foundation. Assessing the costs depends what services are included in the offer and how the cost is divided between individuals and the state. Burnham said it would be fully funded from within the public spending envelope. He said savings from scrapping the state pension triple lock, starting in the next parliament, would be funnelled into the care service.On its own this would not be enough to fully fund a universal NHS-style care service, according to the Institute for Fiscal Studies. It seems probable that raising taxes will be part of the mix. Burnham said a care service would lead to NHS savings by reducing pressures on hospitals. This may free up £2bn a year in the long term, according to the King’s Fund thinktank. But it added that such figures should be treated with caution.Will individuals have to contribute to the cost of care?Under a Scottish-style system, yes. Burnham said a future care system would give people “peace of mind” that it would protect their “homes and their savings” if they needed care in later life.13:38Burnham’s triple lock gamble | Politics WeeklyThis clearly suggests people who do not qualify for state care support will not have their assets wiped out if they require expensive long-term care – though the prime minister did not spell out how this risk would be nullified. It seems probable, however, that individual’s assets would be better protected from care costs under a national care service, rather than being entirely insulated. Even the Danish care system – one of the world’s most generous according to the Nuffield Trust thinktank – expects individuals to pay for care home accommodation costs.Who will provide the care?Burnham was careful in his speech to thank care workers, recognising them as underpaid and undervalued. He apologised to them, saying politicians had let them down for too long. This was not just burnishing his pro-worker credentials but recognising that without a better paid, upskilled work force, providing a high-quality national care service is impossible.It also paves the way for a government U-turn on overseas care worker visas. He said care services would be “for people, not profit” which may be tricky given that the bulk of adult social care provision is privately provided, although it may signal a crackdown on “obscene” care profits.When will a national care service happen?Burnham set out a broad schedule. Louise Casey will produce her independent report on social care in 2027, setting out what a national care service could look like and how it could be paid for.A national care service would be in the next Labour manifesto, and were the party elected it would be introduced in the next parliament. It is a more urgent timetable than his predecessor, Keir Starmer, had envisaged, but some in the creaking care sector will worry it is not soon enough.How much of a political risk is there?Burnham admitted in his speech that he “may pay a political price” on social care but said he was prepared to do so in order to do what he thought was right. It seems unlikely that the Conservatives or Reform UK would support a national care service.But Burnham clearly believes he has the time to “lay the ground” and win over a public that typically has little understanding of the care system or the sometimes catastrophic risks to their family finances under the current system. Last year, Maja T. staged a 40-day hunger strike to protest the "unlawful handover" and "inhumane" prison conditions, an allegation denied by Hungary's prison service.
A Budapest appeals court reduced the jail term on Wednesday for a German non-binary anti-fascist activist's sentence for participating in anti-Nazi violence from eight to seven years.
Maja T., 25, was found guilty in February of involvement in assaults in 2023 ahead of the annual "Day of Honour" in Budapest commemorating Nazi soldiers.
Prosecutors said the activist was part of a multinational far-left group that attacked nine people on the streets, including German and Polish citizens, whom they identified as far-right extremists.
The Budapest-Capital Regional Court of Appeal reclassified Maja T.'s role from co-perpetrator to accomplice, shortening the sentence by one year, the presiding judge said.
The ruling is final and not subject to further appeal.
The defendant entered the court led by guards on a leash amid faint cheers of "Maja" from the audience.
Ahead of the ruling, supporters put up banners near the court entrance demanding the release of the activist, amid a heavy police presence on surrounding streets.
Campaigners, including some German politicians, had questioned whether Maja T. would receive a fair trial, as the groups linked to the attacks were designated terrorist organisations last year by the former nationalist government of Viktor Orbán.
Multiple people accused of participating in the 2023 attacks have been put on trial in Hungary and Germany, with one receiving a five-year prison sentence in Germany.
Italy and France have refused to surrender two suspects to Hungary with courts in both countries citing the risk of "inhumane treatment" in prison.
In 2024, the German Constitutional Court found that Maja T. ran the risk of discriminatory treatment in Hungary as a non-binary person and should not be extradited.
But the ruling came hours too late to stop the handover.

OpenAI is sued over rogue AI Hugging Face cyberattack
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-30
10:16:36 UTC
19:16:36 KST

OpenAI has been sued by a non-profit organization over its models' cyberattack against startup Hugging Face in July.
Legal Advocates for Safe Science and Technology, or LASST, filed the suit in San Francisco Superior Court on Tuesday, in what appears to be the first publicly reported case seeking to hold an AI developer liable for an incident caused by rogue systems.
The cyberattack on Hugging Face by OpenAI agents that escaped their testing environment was one of the first known cases of a model autonomously hacking another company and breaking away from human control to access the open internet.
Other model builders later revealed cyber incidents caused by rogue AI agents.
LASST is seeking an injunction forbidding OpenAI's systems from accessing computers without authorization. The non-profit alleges that OpenAI violated the California Comprehensive Computer Data Access and Fraud Act.
"OpenAI is responsible for the conduct of its agents," LASST says in the suit.
"Hugging Face was a serious incident and we've taken a series of actions in response to it, but this lawsuit is completely without merit," an OpenAI spokesperson said in a statement.
Hugging Face and LASST have been approached for comment.
AI cyber incidents
On Monday, OpenAI said it had abandoned plans to release a new model amid safety concerns.
That came just days after the company said it was conducting an "extensive" review of its models' activities following the Hugging Face breach, after additional examples of unusual or unauthorized agent activity were disclosed, including hacking an Australian government website.
Anthropic's AI systems have also been involved in cyber incidents, including creating fake identities to fool humans.
Nvidia announced it had agreed to pay roughly $13 billion to buy Hugging Face earlier this month. OpenAI had tried to invest $100 million into the startup after the cyberattack, though talks fell apart in the early stages, sources told CNBC.
Hugging Face is not involved in the lawsuit. CEO Clément Delangue previously said in July he asked OpenAI to commit $100 million in compute "to help the Hugging Face community build powerful cyber defenses with the best open and closed models."
"What is critical about the publicly reported rogue AI actions to date is that none appear to have resulted in a confirmed breach of a third party's regulated data," Katie Nadro, partner at Levenfeld Pearlstein, told CNBC.
"When that happens, the breached company will have its own notification obligations under data breach and other cybersecurity or privacy statutes, potentially involving regulators and consumer class actions," she added.
"At that point, the cooperation that has existed between breached companies and AI labs may end, because the breached company will likely seek to recover its financial losses from the AI lab."

During the night of September 30, Russia launched a massive missile-and-drone attack on energy infrastructure in Kyiv and the surrounding region.
Monitoring resources eRadar and War Monitor reported strikes on energy facilities.
During the attack, they tracked ballistic and high-speed missiles heading toward the capital and energy infrastructure.
There were also reports of Russian drones flying toward and descending near energy facilities, including the area around Kyiv’s CHPP-5.
As of 9:30 a.m., the attack was still ongoing, and the air raid alert in Kyiv had not yet been lifted.
Ukrenergo also confirmed the attack’s impact on energy infrastructure, saying some consumers were without power in the morning and that crews had already begun emergency restoration work.
Later, the Ukrainian Air Force reported that during the night of September 30, Russia used Zircon/Oniks anti-ship missiles, Iskander-M/S-400 ballistic missiles, as well as 188 Shahed, Gerbera, Parodiya, and other types of attack drones against Ukraine. Of the drones used in the attack, 86 were jet-powered.
As of 8:00 a.m., Ukrainian air defenses had shot down or suppressed 160 targets, including five ballistic/high-speed missiles and 155 drones.
According to War Monitor’s estimates, Russia used 10 3M22 Zircon/3M55 Oniks-M missiles and another six 9M723 Iskander-M/RM-48U ballistic missiles launched from S-400 systems against Kyiv and its suburbs.
The attack came less than a week after Russia’s previous large-scale use of ballistic missiles against Kyiv.
Militarnyi previously reported that on the night of September 24, Russia launched three waves of attacks on the capital using Zircon and Iskander missiles, as well as attack drones.
According to President Volodymyr Zelensky, Ukrainian air defenses intercepted around 60% of the ballistic missiles used in that attack.

France's CPI to surge 3.0 pct in September
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-30
18:13:41 CST
19:13:41 KST

PARIS, Sept. 30 (Xinhua) -- France's consumer price index (CPI) is expected to surge 3.0 percent year on year in September, up from 2.4 percent in August, according to preliminary data released on Wednesday by the National Institute of Statistics and Economic Studies (INSEE).
In its provisional estimate, INSEE said the rise in inflation was mainly driven by higher energy prices, particularly petroleum products and gas.
Service price inflation was expected to edge up, partly because the seasonal declines in accommodation and transport service prices would be less pronounced than in September 2025. Food prices were also projected to accelerate, particularly fresh produce, while the year-on-year decline in manufactured goods prices was expected to ease. Tobacco prices were projected to increase at the same pace as in August.
On a monthly basis, consumer prices were expected to fall 0.3 percent in September, following a 0.7 percent increase in August. The decline was mainly attributed to the seasonal decrease in service prices after the summer period, particularly transport and accommodation services.
The decline was expected to be offset by rising energy prices, mainly petroleum products and gas. Food prices were projected to increase for the third consecutive month, while tobacco prices were expected to remain stable from August.
The Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices, used for comparisons across the eurozone, was expected to climb 3.4 percent year on year in September, up from 2.6 percent in August. ■

ISLAMABAD, Sept. 30 (Xinhua) -- Pakistani security forces killed three militants in an intelligence-based operation in North Waziristan district of the country's northwestern Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, security sources told Xinhua on Wednesday.
The operation was carried out in Mir Ali area of North Waziristan, where security forces targeted militant hideouts in and around the town, said the sources.
A large quantity of weapons and ammunition was recovered from the militants during the operation, according to the security sources.
The sources added that security forces also foiled an attempt by militants to intercept a truck carrying rations near the main market of Mir Ali area.
Pakistani President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif commended the security forces for the successful operation.
Sharif said operations against militant groups will continue until terrorism is completely eradicated from the country. ■

BEIJING, Sept. 30 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping and other Party and state leaders attended a ceremony to present flower baskets to fallen national heroes at Tian'anmen Square in central Beijing on Wednesday morning.
The event was held to mark Martyrs' Day. Observed on Sept. 30, one day before National Day, the day commemorates those who gave their lives for national independence and prosperity.
Since Martyrs' Day was established in 2014, Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, has maintained the tradition of paying homage to fallen heroes on the day.
The other leaders who attended the ceremony on Wednesday included Li Qiang, Zhao Leji, Wang Huning, Cai Qi, Ding Xuexiang, Li Xi and Han Zheng. They were joined by representatives from all walks of life.

China's express delivery volume exceeds 150 bln packages by late September
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-30
18:13:12 CST
19:13:12 KST

BEIJING, Sept. 30 (Xinhua) -- China's 2026 express delivery volume had surpassed 150 billion packages as of Sept. 29, hitting the mark 12 days earlier than in 2025, the State Post Bureau (SPB) said on Wednesday.
The accelerated pace of parcel flows underscores the resilience and dynamism of China's economy, analysts noted.
China's express delivery sector has grown at a double-digit pace for several years, consistently setting new records. In 2025, the country handled 198.95 billion packages, up 13.6 percent year on year.
This momentum has carried into 2026. Given a steady economy shifting toward higher-quality growth, more consumer demand has been unleashed, providing a solid foundation for the expansion of the express delivery market.
China remains the world's second-largest consumer market and it continues to grow. In the first eight months of this year, total retail sales of goods and services, a major indicator of the country's consumption strength, rose 2.5 percent year on year, with online retail sales of goods and services reaching nearly 13.48 trillion yuan (about 2 trillion U.S. dollars), up 4.6 percent.
Fu Linghui, a spokesperson for the National Bureau of Statistics, said the consumer market is not only growing in scale but is also undergoing transformation, which is mainly reflected in the gradual shift of consumption structure and consumption patterns.
Smart and green products have emerged as bright spots, with wearables and high energy-efficiency home appliances among the fastest-growing categories. Meanwhile, livestream e-commerce and on-demand retail are playing an increasingly prominent role in driving the market's transformation.
The steady growth in express delivery this year also reflects a deeper shift in how China's logistics networks operate. Courier companies are no longer just delivering packages, but embedding themselves into the production lines of manufacturers to boost goods flows via industrial supply chains.
In Ningbo, east China's Zhejiang Province, courier companies have taken over spare parts warehouse operations for manufacturers including Geely Auto, linking directly into their production systems. Notably, the city has developed 282 such collaborative projects between logistics firms and manufacturers, with related business accounting for almost half of Ningbo's total express delivery volume.
Express delivery embedded deep in production chains is becoming a new engine for industrial upgrading, analysts said.
Moreover, China has expanded delivery networks into remote areas to improve public services and unlock consumer spending in the countryside.
Villagers in Changwangchuan, Fangxian County, central China's Hubei Province, once rode electric bikes more than 10 kilometers just to collect parcels, a trek made necessary by the county's mountainous terrain. A new pilot program is changing this, with authorities this year having moved to extend doorstep delivery services to rural communities in central and western China.
This program had covered nearly 3,000 villages including Changwangchuan by the end of August. For residents there, the change has made daily life markedly easier and given local express delivery volumes a measurable boost.
The express delivery industry serves as both a vital artery for the broader economy and an essential lifeline for everyday life, the SPB said, noting that as pro-consumption policies take hold and new growth drivers emerge, the sector is poised to play an even greater role in bolstering high-quality economic development. ■

Ukraine's Foreign Ministry urges international community to demand Russia end siege of Oleshky

"Every day counts in saving people who are starving and dying there. We urge our international partners to act now and demand immediate humanitarian access to end this disaster," Sybiha wrote.
The Ukrainian foreign minister said Russia is planning a propaganda campaign aimed at denying that there is a humanitarian catastrophe in the city.
"According to our intelligence, Russia is preparing to stage dozens of videos in occupied Oleshky, forcing local residents to say on camera that they are happy, well-fed, and grateful to the Russian occupiers," Sybiha said.

- On 28 September, EU chief diplomat Kaja Kallas said that the EU is trying to deliver humanitarian aid to occupied Oleshky.

China will not be first to use AI as weapon, expert says
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-30
10:11:59 UTC
19:11:59 KST

ISTRA, /Moscow Region/, September 30. /TASS/. Artificial intelligence risks becoming a new weapon, but China will not be the first to use it, Wang Huiyao, president of the Center for China and Globalization, said at a session on the sidelines of the 23rd annual meeting of the Valdai Discussion Club.
"We are facing an energy crisis and a climate change crisis. And recently, [the issue of] artificial intelligence has arisen," he said. The expert recalled that the issue was raised during talks between the Chinese and US leaders during Chinese President Xi Jinping’s most recent visit to the United States.
"Let’s not weaponize artificial intelligence. We need to be careful to ensure that artificial intelligence is not used as a weapon. But even if artificial intelligence is used as a weapon, China will not be the first to resort to this weapon," the analyst stressed.
Commenting on the outcome of the visit, Wang also said that "the US and China are now establishing a new balance." "A new round of the trade war has also been postponed because there is no incentive to continue this conflict. The sides have decided to reach agreements through constructive dialogue," he added.
About the meeting
The 23rd annual meeting of the Valdai Discussion Club, titled "Responsibility for the Future: Limits of Possibility or Possibilities Without Limits?", is taking place in the Moscow Region from September 28 to October 1. The club’s flagship conference brings together 120 participants from 40 countries.

Poroshenko urges PACE to maintain pressure on Russia for release of Ukrainian captives
Ukraine
Unknown Publisher

19:11:30 KST

People's Deputy of Ukraine and European Solidarity party leader Petro Poroshenko met with Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe (PACE) President Petra Bayr in Strasbourg to discuss the release of Ukrainian prisoners of war and civilian hostages.
The politician stressed the need to maintain international pressure on Russia to secure the release of Ukrainians from captivity, ensure access for international humanitarian organizations to their places of detention, and hold accountable those responsible for torture and ill-treatment, according to a post on his Facebook page.
During the meeting, the European Solidarity leader also thanked the PACE President for supporting Ukraine, particularly regarding the creation of a special tribunal for Russia's crime of aggression, the international compensation mechanism, and the return of deported Ukrainian children.
The parties separately discussed support for Ukrainian veterans and wounded military personnel, as well as Ukraine's democratic resilience amid the war.
According to Poroshenko, in the context of drafting the new Council of Europe Action Plan for Democratic Resilience in Ukraine for 2027–2030, the talks touched upon strengthening democratic institutions, independent justice, anti-corruption efforts, parliamentary oversight, political pluralism, and media freedom.

An open letter to the honorable people of the United States of America
TEHRAN=The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) has issued a letter addressed to the American people, outlining its views on recent developments and Iran-U.S. relations. The full text of the letter follows:
In the Name of God,
the All-Merciful, the Ever-Merciful 
   
 An Open Letter to the Honorable People of the United States of America
Indeed, God does not alter the affairs of a people until they alter their own affairs.
—The Holy Qur’an 13:11
To the honorable people of the United States of America—the scholars, the students, and the members of the media,
We begin this letter by saluting the noble souls of God’s greatest prophets—Noah, Abraham, Moses, Jesus, and Muhammad, may His peace and blessings be upon them all.
Seven months ago, the U.S. military, launched a war, in violation of international law, against Iran by attacking an elementary school in Minab, murdering 168 innocent schoolchildren along with their teachers. Simultaneously, they attacked the offices of the Supreme Leader of the Islamic Republic of Iran, Imam Sayyid Ali Khamenei, martyring His Eminence and several members of his family, including his 14-month-old granddaughter.
To date, the war has claimed the lives of more than 3600 Iranians, the vast majority of them civilians, including 400 children. Eight universities, three hospitals, and eight schools have been bombed. Yet, despite the unprecedented acts of cruelty and violence suffered by the Iranian nation during this war, the United States and Israel have suffered a crushing defeat, while the Islamic Republic of Iran has achieved a decisive victory.
As the first casualty of the endless wars waged by the U.S. government has without exception been the truth, with the American people perpetually receiving the greatest harm as the result of the U.S. government’s campaign of deception, we wish to highlight some of the facts that are being withheld from the American public. After all, it is the American taxpayers who will have to bear the cost of America’s unjust wars, and so they deserve to know the truth.
Let’s start by considering a few questions. Why has Iran prevailed in its conflict with the U.S., whose military enjoys an annual budget one hundred times that of Iran’s armed forces and possesses a stockpile of weapons and munitions that dwarfs what is available to the Iranian military by an enormously lopsided ratio?
Why do Iranians chant, “Death to America”? Are they hostile to the American people?
The U.S. government claims that the Islamic Revolution Guards Corps (IRGC) is a terrorist organization. Is this true?
Why have the vast and extensive efforts of the U.S. government over the past nearly five decades to restore its domination over the Iranian people continually failed?
Why is the U.S., if the present course continues, rapidly heading toward decline?
How will the present war between Iran and the U.S. unfold and end? How can the American people protect themselves from the consequences of their government’s unjust aggression and shield themselves against the worst harms of the impending collapse?
These are the questions we wish to consider in this letter. We will be candid and forthright. Should you doubt the honesty in the answers we provide to the foregoing questions, you can make a short trip to any part of Iran you wish—possibly even the Strait of Hormuz—and personally ascertain for yourselves the verity of our assertions.
Why Is Iran the Victor?
Why has Iran won the war despite having a defense budget only one percent that of the United States? Perhaps, the first reaction you may have to this question is credulity: “On what grounds do you claim that Iran is the victor?” To determine which side has won the war, we need to see which side has achieved its objectives. American and Israeli officials initially stated that the objectives of their assault on Iran were regime change and partition of Iran. However, after failing to achieve either objective, they started blurting out a changing list of objectives, announcing a new objective with every passing week, and this betrayed the absence of a coherent strategy in prosecuting the war.
The U.S. President has expressed thirteen different targets for the war once the failure of the first two objectives was clear: Iran’s unconditional surrender; seizing Kharg Island and taking control of Iran’s oil; a ground invasion and occupation of Iranian territory; the destruction of all industrial infrastructure; the destruction of all energy infrastructure and returning Iran to the Stone Age; the destruction of Iranian civilization; launching Operation Freedom and taking control of the Strait of Hormuz; debilitating Iran’s economy by preventing all exports and imports; destroying Iran’s nuclear industry; destroying Iran’s missile and drone capabilities; annexing the Strait of Hormuz to U.S. territory and imposing a 20 percent toll; destroying Iran’s air defenses and taking control of Iranian airspace; and ending Iran’s support for Islamic resistance groups in the region.
The United States and Israel expended thousands of bombs and missiles, striking government and residential buildings, dozens of less-advanced and lower-tier weapons-manufacturing facilities, and a number of decommissioned military installations. Yet, aside from damaging several buildings tied to Iran’s nuclear industry and a limited number of air-defense sites, they failed to achieve any of their declared objectives.
Now, nearly seven months into this unjust war, the U.S. military—the largest and costliest military in the history of the world—has scored no wins, and that is all the more humiliating when we consider that it fought the war in collaboration with the Israeli military, which claims to be the
Concrete Evidence of Iran’s Victory
Iran’s victory is not limited to thwarting the enemy in achieving its objectives. The armed forces of the Islamic Republic of Iran decimated American bases located in the Persian Gulf region. Iranian strikes neutralized a significant number of advanced American military assets—including more than 200 expensive strategic drones, 12 tanker and transport aircraft, 30 fighter jets, at least one AWACS aircraft, dozens of helicopters, and dozens of high-value radar and air-defense batteries—and substantially degraded the infrastructure at U.S. bases in the region, destroying more than 350 primary facilities and structures, while the operational capability of 18 U.S. bases was reduced to nearly zero. Arguably, however, the greatest consequence of this war has been the damage it has done to America’s reputation as the world’s sole superpower and the irreparable and gaping cracks it has created in the edifice of U.S. global hegemony. The U.S. can no longer boast of its status as the world’s hegemon. The points we will cover below make this truth sufficiently clear.
More important than all of these, however, are Iran’s remarkable strategic wins.
- The gains the US government had made in its decades-long cognitive and cultural warfare in weakening Iran’s national and religious values and alienating Iranian youth from their cultural heritage were largely neutralized. America’s heinous attack on the Minab Elementary School and its grave miscalculation in aligning itself with the deeply unpopular Israeli regime and martyring the Supreme Leader made the criminal nature of America’s ruling class tangible to the younger generations of Iranians. By strengthening the determination of the Iranian youth to resist and oppose the tyranny of global hegemony, the American-Israeli war reinvigorated the Islamic Republic and ensured that it will thrive for at least several decades to come.
- The media campaign by the U.S. government designed to mislead the American public by stoking hatred against Iran has considerably weakened. Contrary to the best efforts of the U.S. government, Iran’s standing in American public opinion is actually improving, while Americans’ awareness of—and hostility toward—the principal force behind the war, Israel, is visibly increasing.
- National solidarity in Iran has grown significantly stronger as a result of the war. The efforts of the U.S. government at laying the groundwork for the partition of Iran over the past five decades have been foiled, its various ethnic groups being ever prouder of their national identity.
- For the first time in history, Iran has exerted, and retained, operational control over the Strait of Hormuz. Consequently, American warships were forced to flee deep into the Indian Ocean. Not a single U.S. vessel can now dock at the vaunted U.S. Fifth Fleet in Bahrain.
- Not only did Iran retain its missile and drone stockpiles largely intact; it ramped up production of weapons and munitions and, amazingly, developed more advanced iterations even as the war raged on.
- With each passing day of the war, Iran’s air-defense capabilities became more mature and powerful. Iran successfully shot down the most advanced American and Israeli aircraft, including some equipped with the latest stealth technology.
- At the beginning of the war, people in the streets of Manama and Doha witnessed American military personnel fleeing their bases. They were reportedly running around in their underwear, looking for places to hide. In the following days and weeks, official U.S. military statements announced the withdrawal of successively larger numbers of American forces from the region. American bases have come to resemble ghost towns, and there is now serious discussion in the corridors of American power about the dissolution of these bases.
- The war led to a substantial growth in Iran’s support for the Resistance Front. In the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding between the Presidents of Iran and the U.S., American officials begrudgingly acknowledged the inseparable alliance of the various resistance groups within the region.
- Trump did not and could not destroy the Iranian civilization, which now, thanks to the war, shines brighter than ever before. Iran has gained a far higher standing in the eyes of people around the world. The cultural influence and standing of Iranian civilization are far greater than they were before the war. To verify this, you can travel to a few countries and pose as an Iranian, and the admiring welcome you will receive from people of different faith and nationalities will speak volumes.
- Iran’s victory has endowed people all around the world with a heightened degree of political consciousness and a revitalized sense of self-confidence. This will in time serve as a powerful source of change, leading to seismic transformation in how people exercise their will to self-determination and stand up to oppression and injustice.
- The illegal move by the U.S. military to halt the free movement of ships in the Indian Ocean—which the Trump administration misleadingly calls “a naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz”—has in fact led to greater growth in Iran’s domestic production and a sharp boost in its economic engagement with its neighbors.
- The martyrdom of Imam Sayyid Ali Khamenei has shone a spotlight on the concept of wilayat al-faqih (“the rule of the jurisprudent”) in the global arena, introducing the reality of this religiopolitical office to the world and debunking the lies that try to falsely portray wilayat al-faqih as a form of dictatorship. The historic funeral procession of the martyred Supreme Leader, which saw the participation of over 40 million mourners in Iran and Iraq, served as a globally reverberating vindication of the superior moral and political legitimacy of the system of governance at the heart of the Islamic Republic of Iran. Though painful, the martyrdom of Iran’s Supreme Leader did not lead, as American and Israeli politicians had hoped, to the disintegration of the Islamic Republic, and this was a testament to the resilience of a political system rooted in the will of the people.
The martyrdom of Imam Khamenei demonstrated to the whole world that wilayat al-faqih is not an ordinary political office but is one founded on mutual affection and trust between a leader and his people. Wilayat al-faqih is the embodiment of all godly virtues in the political sphere. It was wilayat al-faqih that empowered Iran to stand firm against diabolical powers with incomparably greater firepower by enabling the country’s armed forces to fight successfully using only domestically
produced weapons and munitions; that succeeded in winning the hearts of people around the world despite overwhelming hostility from thousands of media outlets with virtually limitless resources affiliated with the world’s superpower; that ensured that not a single store shelf has been left empty in spite of 47 years of “crippling” sanctions; that facilitated the fastest rate of scientific progress in the world in the face of the most severe scientific and technological constraints; and that makes a leader who is capable of ruling for 37 years while maintaining a lifestyle resembling that of the lower echelons of the society and refraining from allocating any special privileges to himself or his loved ones.
The Main Factors Underpinning Iran’s Victory
The main factor behind Iran’s victory is not drones and missiles. The United States and Israel possess more powerful and more advanced missiles and drones, plus a variety of other forms of weaponry that Iran lacks. The principal reason for Iran’s victory is threefold:
- The Quran’s superior doctrine and worldview
- The Iranian nation’s faith in and unity around the tenets of the Quran
- The competent and righteous leadership of a man of God
- The Quran’s Superior Doctrine and Worldview
Iran is the birthplace of the most controversial and, at the same time, the most misunderstood political revolution in the modern era—a revolution founded on the Quran and the teachings of the most noble of divine guides. In a word, the underlying foundation of the Islamic Revolution of Iran is the Quran’s divinely revealed doctrine and worldview.
Honesty, liberty, equality, social equity, respect for the rights of others, political discernment, compassion, and the priority of human values over personal desires are among the basic social principles that stem from this Quranic doctrine.
The Quran proclaims all human beings brothers and sisters and servants of God. No race, color, ethnicity, or nation is given pride of place in Islam. Humanity is of one cloth, and an assault on a single human being is an assault on all of humanity.
The political philosophy upon which the intellectual foundations of the Islamic Republic are founded is informed by the central elements of the divine mandate of God’s prophets, especially an unqualified trust in God and an uncompromising struggle for justice. The Quran teaches us to neither oppress nor succumb to oppression.
In this light, one of the principal missions pursued by the leadership of the Islamic Republic has been a tireless effort to strengthen Iran, empowering it to protect and promote the Quranic values enshrined in Iran’s constitution and safeguard the integrity and autonomy of the nation against the unrelenting attacks of the forces of evil. Iran’s leaders feel personally obligated to fight ignorance and injustice and defend truth, justice, and freedom.
To surrender to the enemies of truth and justice would mean nothing less than resigning ourselves to the evisceration of the sacred values of the Quran and is therefore out of the question. It is this resolute determination to fight for truth and justice that constitutes the inexhaustible source of the
power that fuels the Iranian nation in its decades-long refusal to surrender, despite the persistent hostility of the world’s mightiest powers.
- The Iranian Nation’s Faith in and Unity around the Tenets of the Quran
The incredible spirit of resistance and struggle that permeates the nation of Iran stems from a deep faith in the Quran. The Iranian psyche is fundamentally shaped by real historical role models who personified the tenets of the Quran—towering figures of godliness who are revered in Iran as legends worthy of devotion and imitation. Any nation that looks up to these role models will undoubtedly be invincible.
Therefore, if you want to know the secret to Iran’s invincibility, you must read about the tragedy of Karbala and come to know Imam Husayn (peace be upon him), the archetypal exemplification of standing up for justice and welcoming death with open arms in defense of the truth. He bravely fought a fierce battle despite his thirst, continuing to fight even after witnessing all his men slain before his eyes, and never succumbing to the forces of evil.

Russia is preparing staged videos with residents of Oleshky to conceal the humanitarian catastrophe — Sybiha

According to intelligence, Russia wants to stage videos depicting well-being in Oleshky. Sybiha called for increased pressure and humanitarian access to be ensured.
Russia is preparing to film staged videos with residents of the occupied city of Oleshky in order to create the appearance of well-being in the city and deny the humanitarian catastrophe. Ukraine's Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said this on the social network X, UNN reports.
According to our intelligence, Russia is preparing to stage dozens of videos in occupied Oleshky. Local residents will be forced to say on camera that they are happy, well-fed, and grateful to the Russian occupiers... This is another step in Russia's disgusting, weeks-long propaganda campaign, which denies any problems in Oleshky and claims that there is no humanitarian catastrophe there
He stressed that Russian cynicism knows no bounds. "First, the occupiers seize the city, cut off civilians' routes out, and block humanitarian aid. Then they force local residents to take part in staged propaganda videos," Sybiha said.
Ukraine's Foreign Minister calls on the international community and all relevant international organizations to increase pressure on Moscow and demand that the Russian occupiers immediately end the siege of Oleshky. At the same time, the Defense Forces of Ukraine are making every effort to rescue people, including the recent delivery of humanitarian aid by heavy drones, the minister stressed.
Every day matters for saving the people who are starving and dying there. We call on our international partners to act now and demand immediate humanitarian access to put an end to this tragedy

The UK government’s “one in one out” deal with France, which was supposed to help deter small boat arrivals, is expected to expire on Thursday, government sources have said.
Negotiations to extend the deal have stalled over French demands for a Europe-wide deal instead, and a reluctance to scale up the numbers of people exchanged between the two countries.
Flights that remove people who have been already detained under the scheme will continue, but they are expected to end within weeks.
A UK government source confirmed that the expectation was that the deal would be formally drawn to a close on Thursday.
“We would like to see the deal continue. But it’s not the end of the world if it doesn’t because it never got to the scale where it would have been a proper deterrent to people coming to the UK in small boats,” the source said.
The French interior ministry told French media on Wednesday: “We are discussing with the British the terms of exiting the agreement.”
Negotiations in Paris over how best to tie up the deal are continuing between Home Office staff and their French counterparts.
More than 1,400 people who have arrived in the UK via small boats have been sent back to France under the deal. As of the end of June 2026, 1,117 people with links to the UK had been sent to the UK from France.
The deal had been set to expire in April but was extended to 1 October to help counter the anticipated increase in attempted crossings during the summer.
The scheme was announced by Keir Starmer and the French president, Emmanuel Macron, in July 2025 and the first flights took off in September that year.
At the time, Starmer described the deal as “groundbreaking” because it would help to deter the number of people crossing the Channel illegally.
“There is no silver bullet here, but with a united effort, new tactics and a new level of intent, we can finally turn the tables,” he said.
Many of the detainees deported to France under the deal have become homeless in the French capital.
Others have returned to the camps around Calais and Dunkirk, and some have made the Channel crossing back to the UK.
In June, France’s interior minister, Laurent Nuñez, lauded the scheme as a potential deterrent but said France was not prepared to go it alone with Britain.
“According to information from the UN high commissioner for refugees, word of the scheme is beginning to spread, which is prompting a number of migrants to abandon their plans to make the crossing,” Nuñez told a parliamentary commission.
“The value of this scheme is therefore clear. Nevertheless, we consider that France should not bear the burden alone and that it would be better to incorporate it into an agreement between the EU and the UK.
“I have therefore already made it clear to my counterpart that this pilot agreement, which we signed in August 2025, was not intended to be extended beyond 1 October 2026.”
An EU-wide returns deal known as the Dublin agreement existed before the UK left the EU. Attempts to continue the returns deal post-Brexit have been rejected by EU leaders.
Shabana Mahmood, the home secretary, disclosed to MPs this month that the deal cost about £56,000 for every person sent back to France.
She dismissed suggestions that an EU-wide system would be a “silver bullet” for the Channel crisis. She said: “It is a real mistake to think that that pact is the future. And if we were in that, this problem would go away, because I promise you it would not.”
She added that the government’s scheme had struggled to scale up to larger numbers of returns and it had been “operationally difficult” to increase removals because of constraints such as detention space.
“It’s not been without its challenges. Obviously, the numbers are still relatively small,” she said.
Between January and 27 September, 19,135 people crossed the Channel by small boat from France. This was down by 42% on the same period the previous year.

Romania Receives First AAV-7 Tracked Amphibious Vehicles from the U.S.
Unknown
Unknown Publisher

19:09:00 KST

The Romanian Naval Forces received the first AAV-7 tracked amphibious vehicles from the United States.
The commissioning ceremony for the first nine vehicles was held at the Babadag garrison, the Romanian Naval Forces reported.
The procurement of the armored vehicles began in 2023 and covered the delivery of 21 vehicles. In 2024, Romania announced plans to purchase another 44 vehicles.
The Romanian government requested to purchase the tracked armored vehicles from the United States in the AAVP-7A1 variant, designed to transport and land troops, AAVC-7A1 command vehicles, and AAVR-7A1 armored recovery vehicles.
The deliveries are planned in two phases: 21 vehicles in the first phase and 44 in the second.
The delivery of the entire batch of armored vehicles to the Romanian Naval Forces is planned to be completed between 2026 and 2031.
The new amphibious vehicles will enter service with the 307th Marine Infantry Regiment Heracleea.
The vehicles will enhance the unit’s response capabilities in the Danube Delta and along the Black Sea coast.
The AAV-7 has a three-person crew and can carry up to 21 paratroopers or five tonnes of cargo. Its turret is armed with an M2 Browning 12.7 mm machine gun and an Mk.19 40 mm automatic grenade launcher.
FMC Corporation began developing the AAV-7 (Assault Amphibious Vehicle) in the 1960s to replace the outdated LVT-5.
Serial production of the vehicle, initially designated LVTP-7, began for the U.S. Marine Corps in the 1970s.
The U.S. is phasing out these vehicles as the Marine Corps actively replaces them with more modern eight-wheeled ACVs (Amphibious Combat Vehicles).

Mediation over Drumcree parade is ‘dead in the water’, say nationalists
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-30
10:06:39 UTC
19:06:39 KST

Talks to break the deadlock over the controversial Drumcree parade will continue with the Northern Ireland secretary, Chris Bryant, on Wednesday as nationalist protesters declare the prospect of mediation with unionists “dead in the water”.
The nationalist Garvaghy Road Residents’ Coalition has at the same time launched a fresh legal challenge to reimpose the almost 30-year ban on the Orange Order marching down their road, mounting fresh arguments that the Parades Commission has “materially misdirected itself”.
Breandán Mac Cionnaith, the leader of the group, said his goal was “no parade, just no parade, that is what our community wants, that’s what nearly 4,000 people living in our community wants … that’s our mandate”.
After his meeting with Bryant on Tuesday he told residents at the local pastoral centre that mediation was “dead in the water”.
Members of the Portadown Orange Order left Drumcree church, the start point for the parade, overnight on Tuesday for the first time since the dispute over their march erupted on Sunday morning.
They made a further attempt to walk the route down the nationalist Garvaghy Road just after 10pm on Tuesday night, accompanied by the DUP MP Carla Lockhart, and returned to the church on Wednesday morning having vowed to remain there until the police allowed them to complete the march.
The Orange Order Portadown district master, Nigel Dawson, said he had “constructive” talks after his meeting with the Northern Ireland secretary over the possibility of a mediator on Tuesday night. “We look forward to the law being applied to the parade,” he added.
The two groups will have further talks with Bryant on Wednesday and the Garvaghy Road court hearing is scheduled for Friday, but there is little sign of a breakthrough.
The high court at a special sitting on Saturday heard that the documentation around the decision to allow the parade showed past risk assessments of disorder in relation to parade requests but none looking to the future.
Under a heading on a form listing any risk of public disorder or damage to property, the commission’s information was “directed to the past”, their barrister, Denise Kiley KC, told the judge. “Nowhere do we see any assessment of future risk,” she said adding that it was “not clear who had provided this template” to the Parades Commission.
Efforts to end the dispute, which has heightened sectarian divisions in Northern Ireland, were also brought to Dublin where Sinn Féin’s leader, Mary Lou McDonald, and the Northern Ireland first minister, Michelle O’Neill, met Micheál Martin and Simon Harris, the leader and deputy leader of the Irish government.
Martin has described the Parades Commission decision to allow the parade march down Garvaghy Road for the first time in almost 30 years as “incomprehensible and wrong”.
McDonald said people were “gobsmacked” by the decision as it had “the potential to drag that community and society back to a very bad and very bleak days”.
O’Neill has faced criticism from unionists after she and senior colleagues were among a large crowd that blockaded the road in the predominantly nationalist Garvaghy Road area on Sunday to prevent the parade from passing the route.
Under parading laws in Northern Ireland, protests must be notified to, and approved by, the Parades Commission adjudication body and the gathering at the head of Garvaghy Road, that continues on Wednesday, has not yet been notified. However, police have not tried to break up the protest, fearing it could trigger violence.
Bertie Ahern, the former taoiseach and co-architect of the 1998 peace deal that led to republicans and loyalists laying down their arms after 30 years of violence, warned of the dangers of returning to the “tribal past”.

Morocco appoints first female prime minister
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-30
10:05:30 UTC
19:05:30 KST

Morocco appoints first female prime minister
Moroccan King Mohammed VI has appointed Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri as the North African nation’s first female prime minister following her party’s victory in last week’s parliamentary elections, the royal palace has announced.
The monarch tasked the 50-year-old lawyer, who served as housing minister and mayor of Marrakech, with forming a new government, according to a statement released on Tuesday.
Mansouri’s liberal-centrist Authenticity and Modernity Party (PAM) won 97 of the lower house’s 395 seats in the September 23 vote and must form a coalition to secure a governing majority. She becomes the second woman to serve as prime minister in an Arab country, after Tunisia’s Najla Bouden, who held the post from 2021 to 2023.
PAM overtook outgoing Prime Minister Aziz Akhannouch’s National Rally of Independents, which won 66 seats, followed by Istiqlal with 65, according to results published by the Interior Ministry on September 25. Turnout fell to about 38%, compared with around 50% in 2021, official figures showed.
PAM was part of Akhannouch’s outgoing coalition government alongside his National Rally of Independents and Istiqlal. During the campaign, PAM ruled out renewing the alliance with Akhannouch’s party, but Mansouri later said she had no “red lines” for coalition talks.
The appointment comes amid an investigation into suspected electoral fraud in the northern port city of Tangier. Prosecutors said a polling-station deputy allegedly removed ballots with the station head’s help before returning them to two polling stations in coordination with other suspects. Investigators found that ink on the seized ballots differed from that used at the polling stations.
Tangier Mayor Mounir Limouri, a PAM official, was placed in police custody on Monday as part of the investigation, multiple outlets reported, citing judicial sources. Five other suspects were held in pretrial detention. Limouri denied any connection to the alleged tampering.
PAM said it would take disciplinary action against members if investigators established their involvement.
Founded in 2008 by Fouad Ali El Himma, a close adviser and childhood friend of the king, PAM emerged as a secular-leaning rival to the Islamist Justice and Development Party.
The constitution requires the king to appoint the premier from the party that wins the most parliamentary seats but the monarch retains sweeping powers over defense and foreign policy.
The new government will oversee Morocco’s preparations to co-host the 2030 FIFA World Cup with Spain and Portugal. Spending on the tournament partly fueled deadly youth-led protests last year, with demonstrators demanding jobs and better healthcare and education. During the election campaign, parties offered jobs and affordable housing to attract young voters after July’s mass border crossing into the Spanish enclave of Ceuta, Reuters reported.
Mansouri has pledged a program offering “concrete and realistic solutions to citizens’ concerns,” acknowledging high expectations, particularly among young people.
